title: Client prompt-bundling telemetry patterns and canonical fixes
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary

This page documents recommended client-side prompt-bundling patterns and the minimal telemetry contract required for robust observability and support. It is intended for SDK authors, integrators, and partner engineers who want predictable costs and clear failure modes while using Redwood’s inference API. The guidance here emphasizes: deterministic bundling keys, telemetry fields required for root-cause analysis, and canonical fixes for the top support issues we see in the field.

When to apply these patterns

- High-throughput text-generation where multiple short prompts are sent within the same request window.
- Applications that need deterministic token accounting and chargeback visibility (e.g., multi-tenant SaaS).
- Integrations that must maintain latency SLOs while applying client-side caching or retries.

Goals

- Reduce per-token compute cost via safe bundling without breaking per-user semantics.
- Ensure server-side traces contain enough context to attribute cost and debug errors.
- Provide a small set of canonical fixes that support can apply without long back-and-forth with customers.

Core concepts

- Bundle: a single API call that contains multiple prompts/inputs from the same logical origin and compatible model settings.
- Bundle key: a deterministic ID describing the reason and boundaries for bundling (e.g., user-session+route+template-hash).
- Bundle size policy: max_prompts and max_total_tokens per bundle to respect latency and memory budgets.

Recommended bundling policy (default)

Table: bundling defaults (safe for most workloads)
| setting | default | rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| max_prompts_per_bundle | 8 | Avoids head-of-line blocking and keeps per-request overhead modest |
| max_total_tokens_in | 1024 | Fits typical 16GB GPU KV cache footprint at 4–8 prompts |
| max_token_ratio_out | 2.0 | Protects against prompts that explode to large completions |
| flush_interval_ms | 30 | Micro-batching window to collect near-simultaneous prompts |

Implementation examples

1) Deterministic bundle key (JS snippet)

const bundleKey = (ctx) => `${ctx.userId}:${ctx.route}:${hash(ctx.promptTemplate)}`;

2) Client-side bundler (high-level pseudo)

- Accept request with metadata { userId, route, promptTemplate, priority }.
- Compute bundleKey and append to in-memory queue for that key.
- If queue length >= max_prompts_per_bundle OR total_tokens >= max_total_tokens_in, flush immediately.
- Otherwise flush at flush_interval_ms or on explicit flush.

Code examples

JavaScript (Node) — bundling + call into Redwood hosted API\n

// simplified example; production SDKs should checksum prompts, handle retries
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });

async function flushBundle(bundleKey, prompts) {
  // compose batch request payload expected by our runtime
  const payload = {
    model: 'open-redwood/small-1',
    bundle_id: bundleKey,
    inputs: prompts.map(p => ({ text: p.text, metadata: p.metadata }))
  };
  const resp = await client.batchGenerate(payload);
  return resp;
}

Python — telemetry enrichment example

# attach telemetry to each request; our observability pipelines expect the keys below
telemetry = {
  "event": "request.send",
  "service": "webapp",
  "bundle_id": bundle_id,
  "model": "open-redwood/small-1",
  "prompts": len(prompts),
  "tokens_in": sum(p.tokens for p in prompts),
  "sampling_policy": "top_p=0.95,temp=0.8"
}
emit_telemetry(telemetry)

Telemetry contract (required fields)

All SDKs and client libraries must emit a single telemetry event per outbound bundle call that contains at least the following fields. These are used by product, SRE, and support for billing attribution and RCA.

Table: telemetry fields
| field | type | example | purpose |
|---|---:|---|---|
| event | string | request.send | distinguishes request lifecycle events |
| bundle_id | string | bundle-20260203-01 | deterministic bundling identifier |
| model | string | open-redwood/small-1 | model name/version |
| tokens_in | integer | 128 | tokens counted from client prompt tokenizer |
| tokens_out | integer | 256 | tokens produced (if available) |
| latency_ms | integer | 210 | end-to-end latency measured by client |
| error | string|null | null or short error label for failed requests |
| sampling_policy | string | "top_p=0.95,temp=0.8" | compact policy to reproduce behavior |
| route | string | /checkout/confirm | logical route or feature name |

Example telemetry payload (JSON)

{
  "event": "request.send",
  "service": "storefront-api",
  "bundle_id": "bundle-20260301-42",
  "model": "open-redwood/small-1",
  "prompts": 6,
  "tokens_in": 409,
  "tokens_out": 812,
  "latency_ms": 183,
  "error": null,
  "sampling_policy": "top_p=0.95,temp=0.7",
  "route": "/checkout/confirm"
}

Transport and batching notes

- Prefer the SDK-internal telemetry emitter to buffer and send in-process rather than fire-and-forget via external HTTP. This keeps traces correlated.
- Include the bundle_id as a trace/span tag so backend traces can be joined with client telemetry.

Top support issues and canonical fixes

1) Symptoms: Unexpectedly high tokens_in and charge spikes
Root cause: Client is bundling prompts across different templates or not computing tokens with the same tokenizer as the server.
Canonical fixes:
- Verify prompt token counts using the SDK tokenizer utilities before bundling.
- Restrict bundle_key to include template hash so mixed-template bundles are avoided.
- Add guard: if tokens_in > max_total_tokens_in, split into separate bundles and emit a warning telemetry event.

2) Symptoms: Long tail latency when a single prompt in bundle is slow to compute
Root cause: Head-of-line blocking due to uneven prompt complexity inside a bundle.
Canonical fixes:
- Set max_prompts_per_bundle to a low default (<= 8) for latency-sensitive routes.
- Allow priority flag on prompt entries; when a prompt is flagged high-priority, flush it immediately in a singleton bundle.
- Server-side: ensure per-item streaming responses (supported in Redwood runtime) are enabled so the client can present partial results.

3) Symptoms: Incomplete observability; support cannot map errors to customer actions
Root cause: Missing or inconsistent bundle_id, route, or sampling_policy in telemetry.
Canonical fixes:
- Make telemetry emission mandatory in SDK acceptance tests.
- Provide clear SDK APIs: sendBundle(payload, telemetryMeta) and validate presence of required fields at runtime (warn and increment internal metric if missing).

Quickstart: integrating bundling into an existing SDK in 8 steps

1. Add tokenizer and bundle utilities to the client runtime.
2. Decide deterministic bundle key primitives (userId/route/templateHash).
3. Implement in-memory queues keyed by bundleKey and enforce bundle policies.
4. Emit the required telemetry event before sending the network request.
5. On response, emit a request.complete telemetry event with tokens_out and latency.
6. Backfill server-side tracing by tagging requests with bundle_id.
7. Add unit tests for token counting and a CI e2e test that asserts telemetry fields exist.
8. Deploy with a feature flag and monitor the following: telemetry.rate, avg_tokens_in, 95p_latency_ms.

Monitoring and alerts (suggested)

- Alert: bundle-missing-telemetry-rate > 0.5% over 1h -> pager to devx oncall.
- SLI: average tokens_in variance < 30% across matching routes (rolling 24h).
- SLO: 95th percentile bundle latency < 500ms for latency-sensitive routes.

Rollout checklist

- Add SDK unit tests for bundling logic.
- Run a canary (5% traffic) with metrics exported to the Redwood Console.
- Verify chargeback dashboard shows expected per-route token distribution.
- Validate that support runbook can reproduce the most common errors using the support repro harness.
- Flip the feature flag to 100% once stability metrics are green for 48h.

Appendix: small-run YAML example (bundle policy)

bundle_policy:
  max_prompts_per_bundle: 8
  max_total_tokens_in: 1024
  flush_interval_ms: 30
  priority_breakout: true

If you are an SDK integrator and want a hand rolling this into your codebase, open a PR against the devx-sdk repo and add a note to the reviewers assigning an engineer from the DevX SDK team.
